hints: Focus on what happens to chlorine itself, it starts as an element and splits into two different products in each case.
Remember the cold NaOH reaction makes chloride, $\text{Cl}^-$, and chlorate(I), $\text{ClO}^-$, so work out those two oxidation states first.
Now recall the hot NaOH reaction makes chloride and chlorate(V), $\text{ClO}_3^-$, and combine all the states from both experiments.
walkthrough:
**Spot the disproportionation**

Chlorine starts as $\text{Cl}_2$, so its oxidation state in the reactant is 0 in both experiments. In each reaction it is both reduced and oxidised at the same time.

Oxidation state rule:
$$\text{oxidation state of Cl in Cl}_2 = 0$$

**Cold, aqueous NaOH reaction**

Cold conditions give sodium chloride and sodium chlorate(I). This is the bleach reaction.

$$\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
In $\text{NaCl}$, Cl is $-1$. In $\text{NaClO}$, O is $-2$ and Na is $+1$, so Cl must be $+1$.

**Hot, aqueous NaOH reaction**

Hot conditions give sodium chloride and sodium chlorate(V). A more oxidised product forms.

$$3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH} \rightarrow 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
In $\text{NaCl}$, Cl is again $-1$. In $\text{NaClO}_3$, with $3 \times (-2) = -6$ from oxygen, Cl must be $+5$ to give an overall $-1$ ion.

**Combine both experiments**

Collect every state seen in reactants or products across the two reactions. We have 0 from $\text{Cl}_2$, $-1$ from $\text{Cl}^-$, $+1$ from $\text{ClO}^-$, and $+5$ from $\text{ClO}_3^-$.

options.A: Correct. Both reactions start with 0 in Cl2. Cold gives -1 and +1, hot gives -1 and +5. Together all four states 0, -1, +1 and +5 appear.
options.B: Incorrect. This lists only the cold reaction products (0, -1, +1). It forgets that hot NaOH produces chlorate(V), NaClO3, where Cl is +5.
options.C: Incorrect. This lists only the hot reaction products (0, -1, +5). It forgets that cold NaOH produces chlorate(I), NaClO, where Cl is +1.
options.D: Incorrect. This omits -1. Both reactions produce large amounts of NaCl by reduction of chlorine, so chloride with oxidation state -1 must be present.
